name: Incessant Infant Ventricular Tachycardia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Incessant Infant Ventricular Tachycardia Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Electrocardiogram demonstrating sustained ventricular tachycardia lasting more than 30 minutes without spontaneous termination
Onset of ventricular tachycardia within the first year of life
No evidence of structural heart disease on echocardiography or cardiac MRI
Partial or complete response to antiarrhythmic therapy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Sustained ventricular tachycardia on ECG lasting >30 minutes in an infant under 1 year old, with exclusion of structural heart disease
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires continuous ECG monitoring and exclusion of other arrhythmia causes.

laboratory: Elevated serum lactate due to tissue hypoperfusion
imaging: Cardiac MRI excluding myocarditis or cardiomyopathy
genetic: Possible mutations in ion channel genes (e.g., SCN5A) in some cases
other: Continuous ECG monitoring demonstrating incessant ventricular tachycardia
Response to antiarrhythmic drugs such as amiodarone or beta-blockers

distinguishingFeatures: Family history of sudden cardiac death
Genetic mutations in RYR2 or CASQ2

redFlags: Sustained ventricular tachycardia lasting more than 30 minutes
Signs of congestive heart failure in infant
Episodes of syncope or sudden cardiac arrest
references: Moss AJ, et al. Ventricular tachycardia in infancy: clinical features and management. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2019.
Orphanet: Incessant infant ventricular tachycardia. ORPHA:45453
Priori SG, et al. 2015 ESC Guidelines for the management of patients with ventricular arrhythmias. Eur Heart J. 2015.
